record.original_question: For a positive integer N, let F(N) be the set of maps epsilon from {1, 2, ..., N} to {-1, 0, 1}; reduce the product over n = 1 to N of ((n+1)/n)^{epsilon(n)} to a fraction a(epsilon,N)/b(epsilon,N), define A(N) as the maximum numerator a(epsilon,N), and set K(N) = log A(N) / (N log N). Determine sharp asymptotic bounds for A(N), or equivalently determine the limiting behavior of K(N), especially improving the known upper-bound strategy for lim K(N).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $N$, let $\mathcal{F}(N)$ be the set of all maps $\varepsilon\colon\{1,2,\dots,N\}\to\{-1,0,1\}$. For each $\varepsilon\in\mathcal{F}(N)$, form the rational number
\[
P(\varepsilon,N)\;=\;\prod_{n=1}^{N}\!\Bigl(\tfrac{n+1}{n}\Bigr)^{\varepsilon(n)},
\]
and write it in lowest terms as $P(\varepsilon,N)=a(\varepsilon,N)/b(\varepsilon,N)$ with $\gcd(a(\varepsilon,N),b(\varepsilon,N))=1$ and $a(\varepsilon,N)\ge 0$. Define
\[
A(N)\;=\;\max_{\varepsilon\in\mathcal{F}(N)} a(\varepsilon,N),\qquad K(N)\;=\;\frac{\log A(N)}{N\log N}.
\]
It is known that there exist constants $0<c_1\le c_2$ such that $c_1\le K(N)\le c_2$ for all sufficiently large $N$ (with current best values yielding $c_2=\tfrac{2}{3}+o(1)$ as an upper bound on $\limsup K(N)$).

Determine sharp asymptotic estimates for $A(N)$. Equivalently, determine the limiting behavior of $K(N)$ as $N\to\infty$: does $\lim_{N\to\infty} K(N)$ exist, and if so, what is its value? In particular, improve the upper bound $\limsup_{N\to\infty} K(N)\le \tfrac{2}{3}$.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2005 Ramanujan Journal paper by de la Bretèche, Pomerance, and Tenenbaum established that $(\log 4+o(1))N \le \log A(N) \le (\tfrac{2}{3}+o(1))N\log N$, improving an earlier lower bound of Nicolas and Langevin to bring it to the same N log N order via the Rosser–Iwaniec sieve. However, the exact asymptotic of $A(N)$, and in particular the existence and value of $\lim K(N)$, has not been determined; the problem is still posed as open.

status_evidence.title: Products of Ratios of Consecutive Integers
status_evidence.snippet: The maximal possible value of a is denoted by A(N). It was known that (log 4+o(1))N ≤ log A(N) ≤ (2/3+o(1))N log N; the authors improved the lower bound to the same order of magnitude as the upper bound using the Rosser–Iwaniec sieve.
status_evidence.claim: Best known bounds give matching order N log N but the precise limit of K(N) is not determined.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Questions
status_evidence.snippet: The problem of estimating A(N) was asked; showing limsup K(N) ≤ kappa would allow further progress.
status_evidence.claim: Determining the sharp asymptotics for A(N)/limit of K(N) is listed among open questions.
